data.hypothesis: Adding the missing <cstddef> include addresses the prior build diagnostic. The resulting candidate tests parallel ownership of independent 32x64 output tiles, using the caller's thread budget, against the previously measured blocked 4x4 microkernel without parallelism. Tile parallelism may improve n=1024 throughput; small cases may see little benefit or overhead. No packing or explicit SIMD is added, so this isolates tile ownership.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use the valid simple-blocked result as a comparison point for this tile-parallel variant; it does not establish the parallel effect.
memory_lessons.claim: The prior simple blocked 4x4 microkernel was correct on all six official cases and measured 0.2830563317 seconds on average. The baseline was also correct and measured 6.4058554967 seconds on average. The new parallel variant has not yet been measured, so these results do not attribute any gain to parallelism.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Validate this build on all official cases and compare repeated native n=1024 timings with the simple blocked result.

data.notes: The previous attempt failed to build because std::size_t was unavailable; this candidate adds <cstddef>. The prior valid blocked result is a useful comparison, but this parallel variant has no measured outcome yet. Controller validation and repeated n=1024 measurements are needed before attributing a performance change.
transformations: Add <cstddef> so std::size_t is declared, fixing the prior build diagnostic.
Assign each independent 32x64 output tile to an OpenMP static-loop iteration, with the worker count capped by the caller's thread budget and tile count.
Retain the blocked scalar 4x4 register-oriented microkernel and first-reduction-block overwrite; use the existing scalar path for incomplete tiles.
Add no packing or explicit SIMD, keeping parallel tile ownership as the experiment's intended contrast.
